result.summary: This PR fixes a shutdown-time crash in IPC mining by making disconnectIncoming() wait for in-flight server call bodies to finish before the node frees state they might dereference. It splits Connection teardown into an idempotent disconnect() method separate from the destructor, adds a ServerObjectTracker to count live ProxyServer objects per connection, and adds Connection::waitDrained() that blocks until that count reaches zero. The IPC-side change then disconnects non-parent incoming connections, waits for them to drain, logs if the wait actually blocks, and only then destroys the connections.
result.problem: IPC-mining nodes can hit an assertion failure (Assert(m_node.chainman)) during shutdown because disconnectIncoming() cancels the KJ promise of an in-flight call but does not stop a server call body already dispatched to a worker thread, which can then dereference node state freed right after shutdown proceeds. This is a real, reported crash (bitcoin/bitcoin#35845, #33387) hitting anyone running the mining interface over IPC.

result.card: Fixes a real shutdown-time assertion crash (Assert(m_node.chainman)) hit by IPC-mining nodes when an in-flight async call body outlives disconnectIncoming(), per bugs bitcoin/bitcoin#35845 and #33387. The fix adds a Connection::disconnect()/waitDrained() split and a ServerObjectTracker in libmultiprocess so shutdown can wait for in-flight server call bodies before freeing node state. It is marked draft because it depends on an unmerged libmultiprocess companion PR (#335), though the author states the code is otherwise ready to review. No reviewer has yet commented (0 distinct reviewers), and CI is currently failing. This is P1 for the ipc category as a stability fix for the multiprocess mining consumer, though it carries stated intentional limitations (parent connection not drained, m_impl destructors not waited for).
